audit_findings.title: Post-anchor convertible financing makes the equity claim internally inconsistent
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,500 million principal; $1,471.731 million carrying debt; $1,469.779 million net proceeds; maximum 5.8932 million conversion shares; carrying debt equals $26.54 per stated diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: The post-anchor financing affects owner earnings through debt-cost amortization, the equity bridge through cash and the senior principal claim, and shares through conversion and capped-call treatment.
audit_findings.evidence: As of the date of this filing, the Company has not utilized the line of credit.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated inconsistency, although the quoted line-of-credit evidence concerns a different facility. The 10-Q shows that the notes were issued after the anchor, while the valuation adds June cash containing their proceeds, does not deduct their senior claim, and uses a conversion-based denominator. The notes require principal settlement in cash, and the capped calls cover only approximately 3.9 million initially underlying shares. The debt omission overstates value, while maximum-share dilution can understate it, so the net direction requires a consistent rerun. The amounts are large enough to materially alter per-share value and the buy-below result.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the valuation on one basis using the May 21, 2026 issuance, $1.5 billion principal, issuance costs, effective interest, mandatory cash principal settlement, conversion waterfall, $88.95 million capped calls, and $204.979 million repurchase; rerun OE, bridge and diluted shares together.

audit_findings.title: The unexplained $720 million stakes bridge may be unsupported or double-counted
audit_findings.magnitude: $720 million, equal to 15.4% of $4,684 million base equity value and $12.98 per stated diluted share; the filed existing non-marketable investment is $8 million and the proposed Rigaku purchase is approximately $710 million
audit_findings.mechanism: An unsupported or duplicated stake directly inflates the non-operating-asset bridge added to operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: During the fiscal year ended January 3, 2026 , the Company invested $ 8.0 million in the equity of a privately-held company.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied record does not support a separately owned $720 million stake at June 30. It shows only an $8 million private investment and a proposed approximately $710 million Rigaku investment expected to close later. The $1,882.15 million cash/STI balance is the pre-Rigaku balance and includes financing proceeds. If Rigaku had not closed, adding its value is premature; if it subsequently closed, its purchase price must reduce cash rather than leave both assets in the bridge. Either case is reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the closing filing and settlement statement, then trace the entire $720 million by security and acquisition date. Replace June cash with the post-closing balance if applicable and verify taxes, ownership percentage, valuation basis and absence of duplication.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains only a stub-period contribution from the acquired business
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified OE impact; filed stub contribution was $8.6 million revenue and a $6.2 million operating loss, while FY2025 pro forma revenue was $81.791 million above reported revenue and pro forma net income was $4.411 million below reported net income
audit_findings.mechanism: The mixed-perimeter anchor can misstate sustainable OE and the growth base for the post-acquisition company.
audit_findings.evidence: From the acquisition date through January 3, 2026, Semilab USA contributed $ 8.6 million of revenue and an operating loss of $ 6.2 million to the Company’s consolidated results.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: the anchor includes Semilab USA only from November 17, 2025, while the valuation represents the post-acquisition company. The filing's pro forma net-income difference is only about 3.2% of reported net income, but net income is not owner earnings and does not establish the acquired business's maintenance capex, working-capital needs or normalized taxes. The record therefore cannot determine whether the current-perimeter OE adjustment is material or its direction.
audit_findings.action: Construct full-year pro forma owner earnings from Semilab USA standalone revenue, operating costs, cash taxes, working-capital investment and maintenance capex, including recurring integration costs; replace the mixed-perimeter anchor and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Nonrecurring acquisition charges may have been capitalized into the perpetual earnings base
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.0 million FY2025 inventory step-up plus $12.5 million acquisition costs, totaling $16.5 million or 11.1% of the $148.2 million anchor; $9.1 million step-up remained after year-end, of which $6.7 million was recognized in first-half 2026 and $2.4 million remained
audit_findings.mechanism: Retained one-time charges depress normalized anchor OE and every forecast period, while omitted post-year-end step-up charges overstate near-term OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The inventory fair value step‑up is non‑recurring and is recognized as an increase to cost of goods sold as the related inventory is sold.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the OE build normalized these items is unresolved, so an actual valuation error is not yet demonstrated. Their filed scale is nevertheless material relative to the anchor. Permanently growing the FY2025 charges would understate value, while excluding the remaining inventory step-up from near-term cash flows would overstate value. Recurring transformation and integration spending must not be removed merely because management presents it as acquisition-related or restructuring expense.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE build line by line to the $4.0 million step-up, $12.5 million acquisition costs, subsequent $6.7 million recognition, $2.4 million remaining balance and recurring restructuring/integration costs; normalize only demonstrated one-time cash effects and rerun the forecast.

audit_findings.title: The historical series mislabels fiscal 2025 as 2026 and falsely treats 2025 as missing
audit_findings.magnitude: one fiscal-year label and one additional fiscal week; correcting the label does not change the $148.2 million anchor, while the base value remains $183.53 per share or 68.5% below the $268.01 price
audit_findings.mechanism: The error affects historical interval labels, the continuity narrative and potentially the placement of the first forecast period, but not the recorded anchor amount itself.
audit_findings.evidence: The fiscal year of 2025 was a 53-week fiscal year that began on December 29, 2024 and ended January 3, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The labeling error is demonstrated: the year ending January 3, 2026 is fiscal 2025, and fiscal 2025 is therefore not missing. On the supplied valuation, growth rates are explicit scenario inputs rather than historical CAGR outputs, and relabeling alone leaves the anchor and scenario arithmetic unchanged. Against the $183.53 per-share base-case price gap, the label correction and one extra week are not capable by themselves of reversing the valuation conclusion. A timing implementation error would be separate and remains to be checked.
audit_findings.action: Relabel the series by issuer fiscal year, flag fiscal 2025 as a 53-week year, remove the false missing-year statement, and verify that the first forecast cash flow was discounted from January 3, 2026 rather than from an assumed December 2026 anchor.
